Our story

Founded on God's Word

Calvary Chapel Longview began as a home Bible study in 1999, hosting its first service in 2001. We believe God's Word is complete and relevant to every life, which is why we teach systematically through the Bible, verse by verse. Under the leadership of Pastor Jason Getzin and our board of elders, we gather twice weekly to worship Jesus and study Scripture together—without pressure, judgment, or compromise on truth.

Good to know

Questions, answered.

What happens during a service?

We begin with musical worship led by a band. Then Pastor Jason or an elder teaches a verse-by-verse study from the Bible with application to daily life. After the message, we have time for response—prayer, communion, or personal reflection.

Is this a prosperity-gospel church?

Absolutely not. We teach the whole Bible systematically and never promise financial returns on 'seeds of faith.' We discuss giving only when Scripture addresses it. You'll never see a building-project thermometer or receive favoritism for donations.

What's the dress code?

There is none. Wear what's comfortable. Our founding pastor wore shorts and flip-flops to church. We're casual in dress and demeanor, but serious about God's Word.

What is Calvary Chapel Association?

Calvary Chapel is an association, not a denomination. Each church is independent with its own leadership and bylaws. All adhere to verse-by-verse teaching and share similar culture, but each is distinct. The association provides exhortation, encouragement, and resource-sharing.

Will my children be safe?

Yes. Calvary Kids is our children's ministry with a priority on safety. We ask families to allow extra time for check-in so we can get to know your children and ensure their security.

Will I feel judged or out of place?

No. We're made up of imperfect people with every kind of story. We won't judge based on appearance, tattoos, piercings, dress, politics, or background. You're welcome exactly as you are.
